details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:~1020-1045 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: `.github/workflows/` changes are treated as unsupported and forced to full review instead of standard tier.
  WHY: Both reviewers tied workflow-only PRs to `scope_state="unsupported"` in `reviewer_collect_review_tier_path_metadata`, which defeats the Phase I contract that standard tier covers allowed top-level directories.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:~1055-1149 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `REVIEW_TIER_LOC` is used in numeric comparisons without explicit validation.
  WHY: If the diff-count helper ever yields empty or non-numeric output, bash’s `-le` check can abort tier resolution before env files are written; severity disagrees across reviewers (nit vs major), so the highest severity is used.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:~1100 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Fallback model-resolution paths can overwrite the original tier/reason snapshot, so invalid-slug cases report the wrong reason.
  WHY: Both reviewers said the later fallback logic can mask the original classification path, making diagnostics less accurate; severity disagrees (nit vs major), so the highest severity is used.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:~1172-1175 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: Unsupported-path full-tier classifications set `REVIEW_TIER_REASON` to `default`, which does not distinguish that trigger from a genuinely broad diff.
  WHY: The tier still resolves correctly, but consumers of `REVIEW_TIER_REASON` lose the unsupported-path signal and can misread the cause.
- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:262 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: `entry_matches()` uses `fnmatch.fnmatchcase()` in a way that does not match the documented globstar-style semantics.
  WHY: Pattern handling can diverge from the help text and admit or reject paths differently than callers expect.
- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:188 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: CLI support for `--allowlist-file` was removed.
  WHY: Callers and tests that pass that flag will fail immediately, breaking the scope-enforcement path.
- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh:395 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The fallback diagnose prompt contract no longer contains `evidence_trace` and `hypothesis` keys.
  WHY: Dropping those keys breaks the Phase D trace/hypothesis contract expected by downstream tooling and tests.
- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh:429 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The static prefix for the diagnose step no longer requires `evidence_trace`, `hypothesis`, or infeasible fallback.
  WHY: Removing the required structure can cause CI failures and weakens the diagnose safety contract.
- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh:689 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The deterministic fallback JSON payload omits `evidence_trace` and `hypothesis`.
  WHY: Downstream consumers and tests expect those keys even on fallback, so the schema is violated.
- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh:734 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The `needs_fixes but empty fix_issues` fallback drops `evidence_trace` and `hypothesis`.
  WHY: The fallback payload no longer preserves the diagnose contract, which can break consumers and CI.
- scripts/ai_memory_lib.py:66 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: `LESSONS_LEARNED_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION` and `record_lessons_learned()` were removed.
  WHY: Downstream scripts still import and call that API, so removing it would raise ImportError and break the lessons-learned path.
- scripts/render_prompt.py:around 877 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: Phase C persona-prefix support appears to have been removed from prompt rendering.
  WHY: Tests expect persona prefixes to be present and idempotent, so removing support will fail CI.
- scripts/label_helpers.sh:66 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The hardcoded label catalog no longer includes `ai:retro`, `ai:security-audit`, and `ai:security`.
  WHY: That breaks contract parity with `.github/ai/label_contract.v1.json` and the label tests.
- scripts/label_helpers.sh:113 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The description map no longer lists `ai:retro`, `ai:security-audit`, and `ai:security`.
  WHY: Automated labeling and contract validation will see drift and fail.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:lines ~1172-1175 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When `scope_state=unsupported`, `REVIEW_TIER_REASON` is set to `default`, which does not distinguish unsupported-path full-tier classifications from ordinary default full-tier classifications.
  WHY: The tier still resolves correctly, but the diagnostic signal in `REVIEW_TIER_REASON` loses the unsupported-path trigger.

Requirement: "add the lite / standard / full review-tier resolver, wire it into review_autofix.yml and the reviewer launcher, skip the consolidator on lite"
Expected change site: scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh (classify_review_tier + resolve_review_tier_active_models) + .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml
Evidence of absence: All three deliverables are present. I verified on-disk: `classify_review_tier` at lines ~1113-1242 of scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh classifies lite/standard/full; `resolve_review_tier_active_models` at lines ~1029-1111 resolves model subsets; `review_autofix.yml` propagates all five `REVIEW_TIER_*` env vars and `FORCE_FULL_REVIEW_TIER` to the codex-agent job; and the lite-tier consolidator skip writes `REVIEW_CONSOLIDATOR_ENABLED=0` into GITHUB_ENV at line ~1224. The cross-pollination claim that `.github/workflows/` changes are unsupported is factually incorrect — the Python heredoc at line 999 explicitly lists `elif path.startswith(".github/workflows/"): scopes.add(".github/workflows/")`.
SEVERITY: NIT
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 1 — requirement satisfied; cross-pollination claim contradicted by on-disk code.

Requirement: "Add a focused resolver test and keep the tier logic limited to the files listed here."
Expected change site: tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py
Evidence of absence: The test `test_review_tier_resolver_routes_lite_standard_and_full_and_handles_overrides` (lines 2548-2654 in the test file) exercises lite, standard, full, force_full, invalid-lite-slug, and invalid-standard-slug paths. The harness function `_run_review_tier_harness` (lines 899-993) is present. Both are wired into `main()` at lines 3730-3741. The test reuses `_reviewer_risk_tier_helper_block()` which spans lines 627-1242 in the script and includes the new `classify_review_tier`, `resolve_review_tier_active_models`, and `reviewer_collect_review_tier_path_metadata` functions (all between the start and end risk-tier markers). Requirement satisfied.
SEVERITY: NIT
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 1 — requirement satisfied.

Requirement: "Keep REVIEW_TIER_RESOLVER_ENABLED=false during acceptance, retain the existing AUTOFIX_SKIP_* fast paths and [force-review] override semantics, and do not rename current reviewer/env settings."
Expected change site: .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml (env block) + scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh
Evidence of absence: `REVIEW_TIER_RESOLVER_ENABLED` defaults to `false` in the workflow env block (line 119: `vars.REVIEW_TIER_RESOLVER_ENABLED || 'false'`). The `AUTOFIX_SKIP_*` fast paths in `review_autofix.yml` are untouched — the gate job's evaluate step at lines 254-779 retains all existing skip logic. The `[force-review]` override semantics are preserved: `FORCE_FULL_REVIEW_TIER` is set to the same value as `FORCE_REVIEW` (line 471), and the new `classify_review_tier` function checks `FORCE_FULL_REVIEW_TIER` at line ~1149 before any tier classification. No existing reviewer env vars are renamed — all five new vars use the `REVIEW_TIER_` prefix distinct from the existing `REVIEWER_RISK_TIER_` prefix. The existing risk-tier resolver (`classify_reviewer_risk_tier`) is called before `classify_review_tier` (lines ~1240-1241) and its logic is unchanged. Requirement satisfied.
SEVERITY: NIT
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 1 — requirement satisfied.

=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:~1149 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `REVIEW_TIER_LOC` is captured from `reviewer_count_diff_loc` and used in numeric comparisons without validating that it is numeric.
  WHY: If the helper yields non-numeric output, bash will fail with “integer expression expected” and abort tier resolution before the tier file is written.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:~1020-1045 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `.github/workflows/` changes are treated as `unsupported_path`, causing workflow-only PRs to fall back to full review instead of standard tier.
  WHY: Workflow-only PRs should qualify for the standard tier under the Phase I contract, but this path forces `full` and wastes reviewer capacity.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:~1100 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `classified_tier` snapshot can be overwritten by later fallback resolution, so invalid model slugs can report the wrong reason.
  WHY: A fallback to `full` can still emit the wrong `REVIEW_TIER_REASON`, making diagnostics misleading.

Requirement: "add the `lite` / `standard` / `full` review-tier resolver, wire it into `review_autofix.yml` and the reviewer launcher, skip the consolidator on `lite`"
Expected change site: scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh (classify_review_tier function)
Evidence of absence: The consolidator skip is correctly wired (writes `REVIEW_CONSOLIDATOR_ENABLED=0` for lite tier), but the path-metadata helper incorrectly treats `.github/workflows/` as unsupported, preventing workflow-only PRs from reaching standard tier.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

Requirement: "Add a focused resolver test"
Expected change site: tests/test_review_autofix_review_p
